note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a UKR 9; A06b UKR 9; L05 UKR 2(1), 19(1), Law on occupied territories April 15, 2014 No. 1207-VII): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Ukraine, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Ukraine for 5 years uninterrupted. Permit to immigrate required. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. No renunciation required if citizenship is lost on the basis of an international agreement. Declaration of renunciation suffices if person is a refugee or performed outstanding services. Declaration of renunciation suffices if person performs military service under a contract in the Armed Forces of Ukraine, is a citizen of an aggressor state or occupying state and has experienced persecution, or is a spouse of such a person. ... Person has voluntarily acquired foreign citizenship after the age of 18. Loss cannot result in statelessness. Persons living in the temporarily occupied territories (Crimea) and who automatically acquired the citizenship of the Russian Federation do not lose Ukrainian citizenship.
